meta.title: Improve list and collection materializers performance
meta.body_summary: Refactor collection materializers to batch-compress elements using gzip+pickle in chunks, reducing I/O operations for large collections especially on cloud storage backends.

perf_labels.notes: Agent implemented batch compression with raw pickle instead of using ZenML materializers; maintainer CHANGES_REQUESTED citing bypass of abstraction layer; PR converted to draft and eventually closed without fix.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 1054 changed lines across 6 files, this is a medium-sized refactor by absolute volume. However, the change was rejected due to a fundamental design issue: the agent bypassed the framework's materializer abstraction by using raw pickle.

review_details.concern_detail: schustmi pointed out that the new code uses pickle directly instead of ZenML materializers, which defeats the purpose of the materializer abstraction. If pickle were acceptable, users could just pickle the whole collection instead of using the framework.
review_details.performance_claim: Batch compression reduces I/O operations from 1000+ to 10-20 per collection, improving performance especially on cloud storage backends.
review_details.rejection_signals: Maintainer CHANGES_REQUESTED with inline comment stating the code is not using ZenML materializers and instead uses pickle for everything, requiring a major rework.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Agent implemented batch compression using pickle/gzip directly, bypassing the ZenML materializer abstraction layer; maintainer required using the framework's materializer pattern, which the agent did not understand or follow.

detection_detail.code_reading: schustmi read the implementation and recognized that pickle was used instead of ZenML materializers, raising a blocking design concern.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No benchmark or performance numbers provided; only narrative claims of I/O reduction (e.g., 1000+ to 10-20 file operations).
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: After CHANGES_REQUESTED, the PR was converted to draft and then closed after ~55 days without any further commits or alternative approach.

core_change_summary.description: In src/zenml/materializers/built_in_materializer.py, replaced per-element materialization with batch compression: elements grouped by type, serialized with gzip+pickle into chunked batch files (default 100 per chunk), added v3 metadata format, adaptive chunk sizing, and cloud storage support via BytesIO buffers.
core_change_summary.secondary_note: The test file contains extensive tests for batch compression and adaptive sizing; documentation files describe the new env variable and usage.
change_trajectory: Initial commit: type grouping and metadata optimization.
Second commit: batch compression with gzip+pickle and chunking.
Formatting commit and cloud storage fix (using BytesIO buffers).
Lint fix and final commit adding configurable chunk size and documentation.
